newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore noon stocks languish, sentiment improves.
newsitem.headline: Singapore noon stocks languish, sentiment improves.

text.p: Singapore shares continued to languish at midday on Wednesday, but dealers noted an improvement in sentiment.

"Sentiment is better although the stocks remain weak. There is a speculative element coming in, led by Van der Horst," a dealer said. The infrastructure firm was up 29 cents to S$2.56 on over 21 million shares traded, despite reporting on Monday an 84 percent plunge in interim net profits to S$4.14 million.
While some dealers hoped renewed speculative fever could help turn the market around, others were cautious due to thin volumes recently.
At 0430 GMT, the Straits Times Industrials Index was down 5.63 points at 2,035.75. Turnover was active at over 102 million shares traded, with 230 gainers to 74 losers.
Small-capitalised stocks like Tye Soon, New Toyo, Raffles Medical Group and Excel Machine dominated trade on selective buying of stocks below S$1, dealers said.

"There is no corporate news on these stocks. They are cheaper for retail buyers than blue chips," another dealer said. Banks were among gainers on institutional buying after the Monetary Authority of Singapore said on Tuesday prospects for financial services remain bright. -- Angela Tan (65 8703083)
